strings.name: Michael E. Mann
strings.summary: Mann moved from physics and applied mathematics to paleoclimate reconstruction, producing the “hockey stick” temperature graph with Bradley, Hughes and others. He taught at Penn State before joining Penn and pursuing public communication. His research faced methodological debate and political attacks. A jury supported his 2024 defamation claim, followed by reduced damages, fee rulings and litigation-conduct sanctions; appeals remained pending. These legal matters are distinct from scientific conclusions.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Studied paleoclimate reconstruction and climate change, advancing public understanding of long-term temperature changes and human influences.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Amherst, Massachusetts, United States; born December 28, 1965.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Long-term temperature reconstruction
strings.highlights.h1.text: With collaborators, used proxy records to reconstruct past temperatures; the graph became an important climate communication symbol.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Berkeley physics and applied mathematics degrees (1989); Yale geology and geophysics PhD (1998, defended 1996).
strings.highlights.h2.title: Research and the public
strings.highlights.h2.text: Studies the climate system and explains human climate influences through books, teaching and public discussion.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Litigation sanctions and appeals
strings.timeline.t1.text: The court imposed sanction-related fees over incorrect loss figures in a trial demonstrative; consolidated appeals remained unresolved at cutoff.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Damages reduction and fees
strings.timeline.t2.text: The court reduced Steyn’s punitive damages from $1 million to $5,000 and separately awarded fees in related litigation.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Defamation jury verdict
strings.timeline.t3.text: A jury found Simberg and Steyn liable for defamation; damages and litigation conduct later received separate court review.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Joined Penn
strings.timeline.t4.text: Joined the University of Pennsylvania and led its Center for Science, Sustainability and the Media.
strings.timeline.t5.title: National Academy election
strings.timeline.t5.text: Elected to the US National Academy of Sciences while continuing climate-system research.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Extended millennium reconstruction
strings.timeline.t6.text: With collaborators, extended reconstruction over the past millennium; results require interpretation alongside data and uncertainty.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Temperature reconstruction paper
strings.timeline.t7.text: Published a multiproxy temperature reconstruction with Bradley and Hughes in Nature.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Berkeley undergraduate degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: Earned physics and applied mathematics degrees before graduate study at Yale.
